correctness.rationale: Reassessed the corrected package in /workspace/repairs/2/. In the frozen wording the t_k values were called peaks, but differentiating Eq. (1) at those phases gives u'=-2λu and r'=λr>0: they are not local maxima. The corrected claim calls them fixed-phase samples and proves the distinction; the exact sampled values and unboundedness are unchanged. Independently, matching the constant, cos(2θ), sin(2θ) coefficients in H'+2λH=2-2h cos(2θ) gives (1/λ,-hλ/(1+λ²),-h/(1+λ²)); at either critical h the harmonic amplitude is 1/λ. Thus r⁻²=2sin²(θ-θ*)/λ+Δ exp(-2λt). For Δ>0 the inverse square stays strictly positive on every compact time interval; for Δ=0 the next zero phase is the first finite escape; for Δ<0 the first zero occurs strictly before the next positive zero phase by continuity. The origin is separately complete by uniqueness. Multiplying the initial Δ by r₀² gives 1-2q₀²/λ. Rotation gives q'=(p+λq)(1-2q²/λ), confirming the invariant boundary; there p'=-q(1+2p²/λ) has constant strict sign. Integrating 2√(R²-q²) over |q|<min(c,R) gives the exact area and 4cR−2c³/(3R)+O(R⁻³); at R=c the excluded boundary has measure zero. For occupation, physical time advances phase at unit speed: each whole-period indicator integral converges by dominated convergence except at the zero phases and level-set equality phases, a finite null set even at R=c. Cesàro averaging plus the bounded last partial interval gives the stated survival law; its c/R term with coefficient 2/π gives an infinite limiting first moment. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed; its finite radius checks are phase samples, not maxima, and its rational identities are tested at sample inputs. The corrected prose, audit and checker description agree with the actual angular-phase test.

value.rationale: The critical blow-up boundary is a natural slice where qualitative infinity portraits do not tell how much physical time is spent at large radius, or how abundant the complete data are in large bounded windows. The corrected result gives both quantitative laws, including a linear area coefficient and a universal critical occupation tail with divergent first moment.
